summary: Attempt 3 closes review-002's delayed-execution causality defect. For new T109 runs, the one existing T061 execution schedule must queue latency/fill under the actual fill-data MarketCursor and apply them only when the main market loop reaches that cursor; no intervening event, callback, risk decision, metric or accounting view may observe the future fill. Audit ordinal and cursor order must agree when created, and publication fails instead of post-sorting a non-causal history. DS-006, ARCHITECTURE, THREAT_MODEL T-22 and T109 now state this rule; T109 acceptance adds the required A(trigger)/B(reactive intervening event)/C(fill) golden case while retaining all T061 frontier, pipeline, failure and determinism guarantees. Pre-T109 artifacts remain unavailable, not reinterpreted. No existing task contract or application code changed.
rationale: Review-002 inspected the current T061 implementation and established that its synchronous future-fill search can mutate the ledger while processing trigger A, before the outer loop reaches intervening event B. Merely binding the saved fill to later cursor C and sorting evidence afterward would create a clean-looking replay that is not the state the original callback at B actually saw. That contradicts exact-run replay. The Owner direction already resolves the choice: T109 must extend/correct the single T061 schedule, not add an engine or reinterpret history. A delayed pipeline is therefore scheduled at C during the original run; at C the market event enters the information frontier, due latency/fill transitions apply deterministically, and only then does C's reactive callback receive state. B remains pre-fill in both original capture and RunState. Audit cursor order is non-decreasing at creation and ordinal is strictly increasing; disagreement blocks publication. Older artifacts cannot prove these historical states and remain explicitly unavailable. All attempt-2 cursor, T104, security, traceability and approved-consumer compatibility work remains unchanged.

impact_assessment.intent: Unchanged: canonical MarketState, exact saved RunState and composed ReplayFrame remain the two-timeline product model. The correction makes exact-run evidence causally true during the original simulation rather than cosmetically ordered afterward; no new product choice or revision change is introduced.
impact_assessment.specification: DS-006 now requires new T109 runs to schedule delayed latency/fill inside the single T061 market loop at the actual fill-data cursor. At a cursor, the market event enters the frontier, due pipelines apply deterministically, then new reactive callbacks run. A/B/C semantics, creation-time ordinal/cursor agreement, publication refusal and the ban on post-sort repair/legacy reinterpretation are explicit. ARCHITECTURE and T-22 mirror the boundary. DS-005/DS-007 and T104/Web semantics from attempt 2 remain intact.
impact_assessment.contracts: No pre-existing contract changed relative to the original A0022 base. Added T109 now expressly extends/corrects T061 scheduling for new T109 runs, retains one engine, prohibits future-fill leakage and post-sort repair, and adds the A/B/C acceptance fixture. The same ten stable impacts remain open; T069's disposition includes preservation of T061 guarantees under the corrected schedule.
impact_assessment.dependencies: Unchanged from attempt 2: T109 depends on T041,T052,T061,T069,T100,T104,T105 and replaces T069/T105. The graph is acyclic. The downstream CONTRACT/SUPERSEDE order and T101/T106/T102 compatibility obligations are unchanged.
impact_assessment.implementation: No code changed. The future implementation must modify the existing T061 execution schedule used by T109, introducing a deterministic pending-pipeline queue keyed by actual fill-data MarketCursor. It must not create another engine. Ledger mutation and latency/fill audit append happen only when the cursor is reached; cursor/ordinal monotonicity is validated as events are created, never repaired after completion.
impact_assessment.data: New evidence records the causal audit actually used by the simulation. At A it records decision/risk and a pending execution; B's captured callback/accounting input and RunState are pre-fill; C records latency/fill and post-fill state. Old artifacts remain byte-identical and exact RunState unavailable; they are not resorted, backfilled or reinterpreted.
impact_assessment.operations: A run with non-monotonic state-changing cursor/ordinal history or early future-fill visibility cannot publish successfully. Atomic manifest/report/evidence behavior remains. Rollback disables new success or restores a causally correct release, never the synchronous predecessor path. Other lifecycle behavior is unchanged.
impact_assessment.security: T-22 now includes future-fill leakage and post-sort laundering of non-causal history. Controls require the one T061 schedule to queue delayed work until the actual cursor and require creation-time cursor/ordinal agreement. Replay evidence still grants no execution or approval authority.
impact_assessment.verification: Author-side investigation only: workflow validate, import-graph, acceptance and git diff --check pass; citation retains only the pre-existing T069 missing-module finding. The new golden fixture uses A trigger, reactive B and fill C, asserts actual callback/risk/metric/accounting inputs at B are pre-fill and equal RunState(B), C is post-fill, original capture equals replay at A/B/C, audit needs no sorting, rerun is byte-equivalent, and all T061 information-frontier, decision-risk-latency-fill, failure, partial-fill and ledger-hash tests remain passing. Independent review remains required.
